title: Can You Paint Over Rust? How to Prep Rusty Metal First
description: Yes, but only after removing loose rust, cleaning, and priming with a rust-inhibiting primer. Paint over flaking rust fails fast in Gulf Coast humidity. Here's the right way to do it.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: yes, you can paint over rust, but only after you remove the loose, flaking rust, clean the metal, and prime it with a rust-inhibiting primer. Paint applied straight over flaking rust will bubble and peel, especially in Gulf Coast humidity where rust keeps growing under the paint.

How to Paint Over Rust, Step by Step

  1. Remove loose rust. Use a wire brush, scraper or wire wheel to take off flaking and bubbling rust down to a firm surface.

  2. Sand the edges. Feather the edges where rust meets sound paint so the new coat doesn't show a ridge.

  3. Clean and degrease. Wash off dust, dirt and oils with a degreasing cleaner, rinse, and let the metal dry completely.

  4. Treat remaining surface rust. For tight rust you can't remove, a rust converter can chemically stabilize it. Follow the product's directions before priming.

  5. Prime with a rust-inhibiting metal primer. This is the step people skip, and it's the one that stops rust from coming back.

  6. Apply two finish coats of an exterior paint made for metal. Spray paint works for small items; brush or spray larger surfaces.

Common Rusty Surfaces Around the House

  • Metal railings and handrails. See railing painting.

  • Metal doors and door frames, especially at the bottom edge. See door refinishing.

  • Garage doors. See garage door painting.

  • Wrought iron fences, gates and patio furniture

  • Rust stains bleeding through siding or stucco from rusted nails or fasteners

Special Cases

  • Galvanized metal needs a primer made for galvanized surfaces. Regular primers often peel off it.

  • Rust stains on siding or stucco usually come from fasteners. The fastener needs treating or replacing, and the stain needs a stain-blocking primer, or it will bleed through new paint.

  • Heavily corroded metal with holes or soft spots should be repaired or replaced, not painted.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use paint-and-primer-in-one over rust?

Not on bare or rusty metal. Use a dedicated rust-inhibiting primer first.

Do I have to remove all rust before painting?

Remove all loose and flaking rust. Tight surface rust can be stabilized with a rust converter before priming.

How long will paint last over treated rust?

Much longer than paint over untreated rust. In our humidity, inspect metal yearly and touch up chips quickly so moisture can't get underneath.
